    -
  • - Tight delimiters. Write {t("{{name}}")}, not - {t("{{ name }}")} — no padding inside the stash. (The parser - requires it for block tags anyway: {t("{{ #each }}")} is a lex - error, so tight is the only form that's uniform across every tag.) -
    • -
  • - Indent with the HTML. A tag's indentation should match the markup around - it — pick 2 or 4 spaces and keep it. Block bodies indent one level past their - opening tag. -
    • -
  • - Block helpers get their own line. Put {t("{{#each}}")}, - {t("{{#if}}")}, and friends on a line by themselves rather than - inlining them mid-markup. As a bonus, a block tag alone on its line is - standalone: the engine trims that whole line, so the output stays tidy. -
    • -
  • - Close tags align with their opener. Every {t("{{/if}}")} / - {t("{{/each}}")} sits on its own line, indented to match the - {t("{{#…}}")} it closes — the body is what's indented between them. -
    • -
  • - Comment with {t("{{! … }}")}, not <!-- … -->. - A Handlebars comment is dropped before render, so template notes never leak into - the output; an HTML comment ships to the browser. -
    • -
  • - Reach for ~ sparingly. A tilde ({t("{{~name~}}")}) - trims the whitespace next to a tag — useful when readable indentation would - otherwise show up in the output, but easy to overuse into line-noise. Format for - humans first; add tildes only where the output genuinely needs them. -
